title: Diego Costa
summary: This document is a comprehensive biographical article about Diego Costa, the Brazilian-born Spanish former professional footballer who played as a striker. The article opens with an overview of his career, including his beginnings in Brazil, move to Braga in Portugal, spells with Atlético Madrid (where he won La Liga titles, a Copa del Rey, and European trophies), a transfer to Chelsea in 2014 where he won two Premier League titles and a League Cup, and his later career with Atlético Madrid, Atlético Mineiro, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Botafogo, and Grêmio before his retirement. An "Early life" section details his upbringing in Lagarto, Sergipe, Brazil, his family, his amateur beginnings at Barcelona Esportivo Capela, and his discovery by agent Jorge Mendes. The "Club career" section chronologically covers his loans at Penafiel, Celta Vigo, Albacete, and Valladolid; his breakthrough at Atlético Madrid (2010–2014), including the 2013–14 title-winning season and Champions League final; his Chelsea years (2014–2018) with detailed season-by-season accounts of goals, honours, disciplinary incidents, and his falling-out with manager Antonio Conte; his return to Atlético Madrid; and his later spells in Brazil and England. The "International career" section describes his two caps for Brazil in 2013, his controversial switch of allegiance to Spain, his debut in 2014, and his participation in the 2014 and 2018 FIFA World Cups. A "Player profile" section analyzes his style of play—his strength, physicality, finishing, and role as a target-man—along with praise from managers and pundits, plus a subsection on his discipline problems, controversies, and reputation for provoking opponents. The document concludes with his career statistics (club and international), a full list of honours and individual awards, records, related lists, references, and external links.
